prompt: [Full submission checklist pasted] Individualtests/<student-name>/ — unit tests ... Individualai/<student-name>/ai-logs/ ... Individualai/<student-name>/ai-reflection.md
output: Read the submission spec and matched existing teammate conventions exactly: tests/Matthias and tests/ryan both use a plain-Node script runner (no test framework) with helpers.js (api()/setup()/ctx), per-area test files exporting [name, fn] arrays, and a test-<name>-endpoints.js entrypoint. Built the same structure for tests/xinying/: helpers.js, test-programmes.js, test-routes.js, test-delegates.js, test-attendance.js, test-ready.js, test-xinying-endpoints.js.
decision: accepted and edited. The AI proposed a jest-style runner at first; rejected that and matched the repo's existing plain-Node convention so the suite is consistent with teammates and runs with a single node command.

prompt: Write unit tests for Xin Ying's programme creation & attendance module covering programmes, routes, delegates, attendance, ready-to-depart.
output: Authored 34 endpoint tests. The suite sets up its own fresh programme/route/delegate per run via helpers.setup() (unique programme name per timestamp so repeated runs don't clash) and asserts on HTTP status plus response shape. Enforced the module's single-route rule in a test (PUT routes with 2 routeIds must 400).
decision: accepted and edited. Rejected the AI's first draft that reused a fixed programme id — a leftover between runs caused flaky state. Edited to create a fresh programme per run so the suite is idempotent.

prompt: [test run output] 'POST /programmes/:id/delegates (empty body)' returned HTTP 500 but controller has a branch returning 400.
output: Diagnosed the mismatch: the controller's catch-guard compared against err.message === 'Provide delegates array, delegateId, or name' but the model throws 'Provide delegates array, delegateIds, delegateId, or name' — a stale guard string. Fixed the controller to match the real thrown message so empty-body add-delegate returns the intended 400.
decision: accepted. This was a real latent bug in the module surfaced by the new tests. Edited src/server/modules/programmes/delegates.controller.js and asserted the corrected 400 status in test-delegates.js.

prompt: [test run output] 'attendance summary has correct counts' failed: byRoute showed checkedIn=2 for a route whose total=1.
output: Traced the root cause with direct SQL probes: the route checked_in subquery joins attendance_records ar JOIN route_members rm ON rm.delegate_id = ar.delegate_id without constraining ar.programme_id = rm.programme_id. A delegate present in two programmes was double-counted on any shared route. Fixed all four occurrences in db.cjs to add AND rm.programme_id = ar.programme_id.
decision: accepted. This was a genuine cross-programme double-counting bug in the attendance summary, found purely because the test creates two runs with the same participant. Confirmed the corrected summary returns checkedIn=1 for the route. The subquery fix was written into db.cjs (the running server) and later replicated to main.

prompt: Which test failures were bugs vs test-logic mistakes?
output: Classified each failure: (1) summary test expected the delegate still on Coach A but an earlier suite moved them to Coach B — test-logic bug, fixed by updating ctx.routeId after the move; (2) ready-to-depart default test asserted a routeId field the endpoint does not return — test-logic bug, removed the assertion; (3) the checkedIn double count — real data bug, fixed in db.cjs.
decision: accepted. I used the classifier to avoid over-fixing: only the summary double-count and the stale guard string were real code bugs; the other two were corrected in the tests, not the product.
